title: First call -> Scale: Hosted API messaging & quickstart hooks
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a lightweight, tactical playbook for messaging the Hosted API to engineers and product teams. Goal: get from first API call -> meaningful evaluation -> production pilot with minimal friction. Focus is developer-first language, predictable cost framing, and quick wins for CTO/eng leads to sign internal POC.

Target audience (short):
- Individual engineer or full-stack dev building a feature proof-of-concept
- Platform/infra engineer evaluating endpoints for integration and scale
- Product manager owning an experiment (NPS/chatbot/assistant)

One-line lead concepts (pick one per asset):
- "Call in minutes. Ship with confidence."
- "Production-grade LLM inference without the infra lift."
- "Predictable performance, transparent pricing — built for engineers."

Core developer-first value props (short bullets for copy):
- Instant integration: simple REST/SDK, sample apps that return useful outputs in <3 minutes.
- Predictable latency & cost: per-route performance profiles and per-token cost visibility in the console.
- Local-to-prod parity: same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — no rewrite when you scale.
- Safety & data controls: request-level logs, optional redaction, and keys you control for private deployments.
- Turn-key fallbacks: automatic failover to a compatible model variant to keep user flows online.

Quickstart angles (3 tiers for docs/marketing assets):
- "Minute-to-first-call" (developer blog + README snippet): cURL + JS client, sample prompt for a helpdesk summarizer, show streaming response. Minimal auth: demo key with time-limited sandbox. Outcome: first token returned.
- "30-minute POC" (guide + repo): integrate a single endpoint into an existing microservice, add basic caching + token budget, show tracing to debug latency. Outcome: measurable latency and per-action cost in dev account.
- "1-day pilot" (playbook for Eng + PM): define success metrics (latency < 250ms p95, cost/unit target), run A/B vs baseline model or rule system, include rollback plan + canary route. Outcome: decision for Dedicated or committed burst.

Pricing-language drafts (tone: transparent, engineering-friendly):
- Headline: "Pay for what you use. Know what it costs."
- Core lines: "Per-token pricing with per-route breakdowns. Optional committed credits for predictable tests and burst capacity."
- Developer tier: "Free tier for experimentation — limits on concurrent requests and monthly token budget; ideal for prototypes and internal demos."
- Pilot/Reserved framing: "Reserved baseline capacity for predictable latency and capacity; billed as monthly commitment with flexible burst credits."
- Short example blurb: "A text generation route at $X/1K tokens + streaming charges; with reservations you can lower effective unit cost by Y% while keeping instant fallback to hosted variants."
- Avoid: heavy legalese; keep pricing copy concrete with quick math examples on the pricing page.

Competitive assessment (notes for engineers + GTM):
- Categories of competitors: large cloud provider managed endpoints; general-purpose LLM APIs; self-hosted runtime vendors.
- Strengths to call out: unified runtime across modes (hosted -> private), production-first SLOs and routing policies, per-route observability that surfaces token breakouts.
- Typical competitor shortcomings to cue in content: opaque latency under load, coarse-grained billing, weak fallback/rollout tooling, poor prefix caching suggestions.

Objections & short rebuttals (for sales/landing page microcopy):
- "We can self-host cheaper." → "Possibly, but infra ops and model ops cost add up. Redwood gives you immediate throughput and ops primitives so your team stays focused on product."
- "Vendors lock us into proprietary APIs." → "Same API across hosted/dedicated/private means you keep flexibility when you need it — not vendor lock-in."
- "How can we trust latency under load?" → "Per-route profiles + canary rollouts + SLA-backed reserved capacity. We surface p95/p99 in the console so you can validate quickly."

Assets to produce (prioritized):
1) Lightning quickstart README + GitHub starter app (3-minute demo).
2) 30-min POC cookbook: integration, caching, budget alerts.
3) Engineering one-pager for CTOs: latency/cost tradeoffs + a pilot checklist.
4) Pricing explainer page: worked examples and calculator widget.
5) Short technical benchmark doc: p50/p95 across sample models and sequence lengths.

Tone and microcopy examples (snippets):
- CTA: "Start a free sandbox — first request in minutes."
- Feature line: "Instrumented per-route tracing to find invoice spikes before they surprise you."
- Pricing micro: "Reserved baseline: commit to a predictable monthly token volume; keep burst credits for spikes."

Open questions / decisions we need from product/legal before finalizing copy:
- Exact free-tier token allotment and constraints (JIRA-GTM-789).
- Whether we publish specific baseline prices or ranges on initial marketing pages (legal & finance input required).
- Standard pilot contract language for reserved capacity trials (product + legal).

Next steps (owner: Asha):
- Build 3-minute README + sample app (owner: Liam). Target ship: 2026-03-10 internal demo.
- Draft pricing examples with finance (owner: Marina). Target: 2026-03-17.
- Create landing page hero + supporting docs (owner: GTM content).

Notes to self: keep the copy engineer-forward, avoid generic "AI" blurbs, surface measurable metrics early (latency, cost per request), and use concrete quickstarts to get them into an account where tracing + cost tools sell themselves.
